comments.body:
Phase 1 RCA — confirmed test-oracle defect; production fail-closed semantics remain authoritative.

Mechanism: tests/unit/test_authorship_batched_ticket_map_7084.py::_fixture_batched_map retries the batched resolver up to five times, but each equivalence assertion then calls authorship.resolve_event_commit exactly once (lines 247 and the base sweep at 209). resolve_event_commit is an authorship/era proof resolver whose contract at src/rebar/attest/authorship_resolution.py:21-23 is deliberate: any git nonzero, no match, missing git, timeout, or exception returns None and never raises. Downstream live-event verification treats an unresolvable introducing commit as fail-closed (verify_authorship.py:243-257), so changing production to treat a transient as proof would be wrong. A bounded retry could preserve final fail-closedness, but rc=0/empty conflates a genuine no-match with a transient and each narrow history walk is documented at 6.78s on the live 71k-commit store; retrying production no-match would multiply the fallback cost without a reliable transient classifier.

Discriminating runtime reproduction used a real temporary tickets Git repo and real event commit. The batched map resolved f4d016a..., then a one-shot injected rc128 on only the per-event git-log made resolve_event_commit return None; an immediate identical second call returned f4d016a.... Thus equivalence was False on the first environmental read and True on replay, ruling out topology, parser, pathspec, and attribution defects. This exactly matches CI change 1837: batched side recovered, oracle side returned None.

Legitimacy: defect in the test harness, not production behavior. Prior closed bug innovative-dandruffy-deer explicitly established the same boundary: fixture-only bounded recovery, production authorship fail-closed/fallback unchanged. There is therefore no unresolved design choice requiring escalation.

Caller gate: production callers rely on None as fail-closed evidence and must not change. Repair is confined to the equivalence oracle: bounded exact retries for the per-event expected value, return only on a non-None SHA, and loud bounded diagnostics on persistent failure. Existing exact position-to-SHA assertions stay intact; no production source changes.

comments.body:
Final rebar-debug report

Problem: the batched-map transient recovery test could recover its batched Git walk, then compare the exact SHA against None from a one-shot per-event oracle read.

Proven root cause: this was a test-oracle defect. Production resolve_event_commit deliberately maps every Git error, empty result, timeout, and exception to None (src/rebar/attest/authorship_resolution.py:8-65), and live authorship classification retains fail-closed behavior for an unresolved commit (src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:243-257). The fixture retried the broad walk but not the narrow per-event equivalence oracle.

Proof: in a disposable real Git repo, the batched map returned the exact event SHA; one injected per-event rc128 produced None on the first resolve_event_commit call, and an immediate identical second call returned the exact SHA. This ruled out topology, parser, pathspec, and attribution defects.

Test: the final held-out oracle strengthened tests/unit/test_authorship_batched_ticket_map_7084.py:233-274 to inject one transient into both broad and narrow real git-log calls for rc128, rc0/empty, and BlockingIOError(EAGAIN). It was legitimately RED before repair (3 failed, exact SHA versus None), GREEN after restoration (4 focused tests passed), and an exact-defect mutation routing the assertion back to the one-shot resolver returned it to RED (3 failed). The persistent case at lines 298-319 proves exactly five attempts and fsck/count-objects diagnostics. The oracle asserts observable exact SHAs, so behavior-preserving refactors do not break it.

Fix: added the test-local _fixture_per_event_commit helper at lines 199-216, returning only an exact non-None SHA after at most five identical attempts and failing loudly with object-store forensics. Every direct batched/per-event equivalence assertion in the module now uses it, including the off-first-parent and ledger-parity cases. Production code is unchanged.

Validation: target module 13 passed; adjacent authorship/identity/compaction selection 38 passed; make lint PASS; make typecheck PASS; git diff --check PASS. The final formatter-only adjustment was followed by another target-module run: 13 passed.

Scope and safety: only tests/unit/test_authorship_batched_ticket_map_7084.py changed. The repair strengthens the existing exact equivalence oracle, creates no production capability, adds no dependency, removes no exact assertion, and preserves the intentional production fail-closed contract.

Siblings: construct sweep found no remaining direct resolve_event_commit equivalence assertions in this module; all route through the bounded helper. Production callers were intentionally excluded because they depend on fail-closed None semantics. Parity census is N/A: this is a test-local oracle seam, not a CLI/MCP/library/automation or dual-direction product operation.

Residual risk and prevention: accepted—the production resolver cannot distinguish transient rc0/empty from a genuine no-match, and one narrow walk is documented at 6.78s on a 71k-commit history (authorship_resolution.py:21-30); production retry would multiply genuine no-match cost, so recovery remains fixture-only and bounded. No other observed fragility remains undispositioned.

Replication: the original one-shot broad+narrow transient scenario now passes for all three failure modes against unchanged real fixture history.

## Context
CI change 1837 failed the authorship batched-map equivalence test after the batched side recovered from a transient Git read but the one-shot per-event oracle returned None. Phase 1 proved production `resolve_event_commit` is intentionally fail-closed and must remain unchanged; prior closed bug `innovative-dandruffy-deer` established fixture-only bounded recovery as the project contract.

## Plan
- Add a test-local bounded helper for the per-event equivalence oracle, mirroring the established five-attempt batched fixture helper.
- Exercise the real temporary Git topology while injecting one transient only at the per-event subprocess boundary; require exact position-to-commit equivalence after recovery.
- Keep persistent failure finite and loud with the existing object-store forensics.
- Route every equivalence assertion in this fixture module through the shared oracle helper without weakening exact SHA expectations.
- Leave all `src/rebar` production fail-closed behavior unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] One-shot rc128, rc0/empty, and BlockingIOError(EAGAIN) failures on the per-event oracle each recover on an identical retry against unchanged real fixture history.
- [ ] A persistent per-event failure stops after exactly five attempts and raises diagnostics containing fsck and count-objects evidence.
- [ ] Every batched/per-event equivalence assertion still compares exact non-None position-to-SHA values, including the off-first-parent case.
- [ ] No production source file changes and `resolve_event_commit` retains its documented fail-closed contract.
- [ ] Held-out RED, GREEN, exact-defect mutation back to RED, focused tests, lint, typecheck, LLM-Review +1, and Verified +1 are recorded before merge and close.
